jurisdiction.venue: Southwark Crown Court & High Court of Justice, London

headline: Seven Years After Skipping Its Bribery Settlement Tab, U.K. Seismology Firm Gets a New Payment Plan
deck: Southwark Crown Court approved a variation to Güralp Systems Limited’s 2019 Deferred Prosecution Agreement, ordering £2.5 million including interest and Serious Fraud Office legal costs—with prosecution deferred unless it defaults again.

live_updates.text: Southwark Crown Court approves DPA variation requiring Güralp Systems Limited to pay £2.5 million including up to £400,000 in interest and S.F.O. legal costs.
First £400,000 installment is due Dec. 1, 2026, paired with clauses barring removal of company assets or intellectual property.
Variation closes a two-year S.F.O. breach battle after the High Court ruled in January and February 2026 that the 2019 agreement remained enforceable.

score_provenance.rationale: Güralp Systems accepted corporate bribery charges and now faces £2.5 million (~$3.17M, or 120.8% of the £2.07M unlawful gross profit) including interest and costs, but paid zero punitive fine above disgorgement, avoided corporate conviction despite a five-year default, and saw zero prison sentences.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Seven years after signing a 2019 UK DPA accepting bribery charges and £2.07M disgorgement without paying, Güralp Systems received a court-approved variation requiring £2.5M (with interest and SFO costs) starting Dec. 1, 2026, with zero criminal conviction.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Ignoring a £2,070 court-ordered criminal restitution bill for five years and litigating whether the order expired
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate default warrant, contempt proceedings, and revocation of suspended sentence
